findings.reason: the author should cite `bench.py`, reuse its tool definition and JSON-arguments check (or state why a validation-time probe cannot call the benchmark helper), otherwise a second tool-call client is maintained beside the first.
findings.text: §3 proposes a tool-call probe ("a chat request offering one tool must come back as a parsed `tool_calls` entry with arguments that parse as JSON") while `bench.py` already ships exactly that: a `tool_use` prompt category offering the `get_weather` function (`bench.py:202`), a request through `_chat(..., tools=tools, ...)` (`bench.py:1280`), and the validation that `msg.get("tool_calls", [])` is non-empty and that `json.loads(tc["function"]["arguments"])` succeeds (`bench.py:1297`, `bench.py:1316`). The second probe (Anthropic `tool_use` block) has no existing owner, but the OpenAI-dialect probe is a re-implementation. Neither §3's prose nor its write paths (`cli.py`, `serve_probe.py`, `test_agent_serve_probe.py`) cite `bench.py`, so the plan gives no account of the search for this mechanism.

findings.reason: the plan must name the durable, time-stamped store `release_at` reads (or drop the function and describe the join differently), or the first implementation node will invent a history mechanism the plan never sized.
findings.text: §4 states "The join has one owner, `registry.release_at(engine_id, when)`, which returns the release of the registration serving that engine at that instant", and its done-when requires `release_at` to distinguish two registrations of one engine (September then 1017) by time. Nothing in `registry.py` can answer that: `ServeRegistration` (`registry.py:106`) has no timestamp. `_record_path` stores one file per job, keyed `<job_id>.json` (`registry.py:301`), `write_registration` overwrites that same path on every write (`registry.py:307`), and `remove_registration` unlinks it when the job ends (`registry.py:363`). So the store holds only current/stale live registrations, not a time-indexed history, and `release_at` has no owner to extend — it would be a thin façade demanding a new history store the plan does not name.

findings.reason: the field should be named for what it holds (`weights_revision`/`weights_commit`), as the plan itself reasons on the `served-name` decision that a name must not be overloaded; a third meaning of `release` on the registration object invites a reader to confuse a held allocation with a weights commit.
findings.text: §4 puts a `release` field carrying `<hf_repo>@<revision>` on `ServeRegistration` and `PublishedEndpoint`, but "release" is already load-bearing twice in this same subsystem with different meanings: `release_registration` (`registry.py:320`) means "clear the hold on a validated allocation" and is already a public subcommand (`registry.py:779`), and clive's `release_id = item["id"]` (`clive.py:277`, `discover_routing_origins` at `registry.py:701`) means "a served endpoint/model id". The plan edits `registry.py` and `slurm.py` — the two files where the first meaning lives — while adding the third.

findings.reason: the interface_budget rule is that an adding section says in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; §2, §3 and §4 each add surface and none does.
findings.text: §2 adds a `revision` field to `ModelConfig` (`imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:25-45` currently carries `name`, `hf_repo`, `served_name`, `size_gb`, `max_context`, `checkpoint_precision`, `weights_slug`, `tokenizer_source_slug`) and passes it as a new `--revision` argument in `generate_download_script` (`imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:1176`, which today passes only `hf_repo`, `--local-dir` and `--max-workers`). The section names nothing it retires or merges, and does not state why nothing can be. Whether the new field is a `public_definitions` addition is the author's call, but the section adds surface without accounting for it.

findings.reason: each adding section must account for the surface in its own text; §2–§4 currently leave three new surface families unaccounted for against a 0/0/0/0 budget.
findings.text: §4 adds a public function `registry.release_at`, a `release` field on `ServeRegistration` and on the published endpoint, and §3 adds a new public module `imas_ambix/agent/serve_probe.py`; none of the three sections names an interface it retires or merges, or states why none can be — even though §3 itself observes that the existing `validate` callback is the extension point and the last commit in this tree (`7ed95902 docs(plans): cover restart's overlap path…`) shows this surface is actively growing.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4's `registry.release_at(engine_id, when)` promises a time-indexed join over registration history, but `registry.py` stores one record per `job_id` with no timestamp field and removes records at cleanup, so the interface names no store holding the behaviour it must hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 adds a third meaning of "release" inside one subsystem: `registry.release_registration` (`registry.py:320`) already releases a held allocation, and clive's "release id" (`clive.py:277`) already names a served endpoint, so `<hf_repo>@<revision>` collides with both.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a `ModelConfig.revision` field, §4 adds a `ServeRegistration.release` field plus the public function `registry.release_at`, and §3 adds the public module `imas_ambix/agent/serve_probe.py`, and no section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 adds `imas_ambix/agent/serve_probe.py` for a chat-with-tool probe whose request-and-parse behaviour already exists as `bench.py`'s `tools` category, and neither §3's text nor its write paths cite `imas_ambix/agent/bench.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 extends the existing profile/download-script generator and §3 extends the existing `validate` callback at `imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:2641` (`run_reload`/`run_overlap` already take `validate`), so neither adds a parallel path; they extend the mechanism they resemble.
